ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure 1, point $P$ is a moving point on the edge of rectangle $ABCD$. Point $P$ starts from $A$ and moves along the four edges of the rectangle, finally returning to $A$. Suppose the distance traveled by point $P$ is $x$, and the area of $\triangle ABP$ is $y$. Figure 2 is the graph of function $y$ as $x$ varies. Then, what is the length of the diagonal $BD$ of rectangle $ABCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to Figure 2, it is known that $AB=5$,\\
when $P$ moves to point $C$,\\
$y=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC=10$,\\
$\therefore \frac{1}{2}\times 5\cdot BC=10$,\\
$\therefore BC=4$,\\
$\because$ the diagonals of a rectangle are equal,\\
$\therefore BD=AC=\sqrt{5^{2}+4^{2}}=\sqrt{41}$.\\
Hence, the answer is: $BD=\boxed{\sqrt{41}}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: According to Figure 2, $AB=5$. When $P$ moves to point $C$, $y=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC=10$, so $\frac{1}{2}\times 5\cdot BC=10$, hence $BC=4$. Since the diagonals of a rectangle are equal, $BD=AC=\sqrt{5^{2}+4^{2}}=\sqrt{41}$. Therefore, $BD=\boxed{\sqrt{41}}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In Figure 1, in rectangle ABCD, A is at the lower left corner, B is at the lower right corner, C is at the upper right corner, and D is at the upper left corner; point P is located on the side of the rectangle, and the arrow shows P starting to move from A along the direction of AB. Figure 2 is a broken-line graph of y changing with x: the initial segment of the graph is on the x-axis, that is, y=0, until the marked x=5; afterward the graph rises to the maximum height y=10 marked by the dashed line, and has a horizontal maximum-value plateau, and finally descends back to the x-axis.

Reasoning: When P moves from A along AB to B, P is always on AB, so the area of triangle ABP is 0. Therefore, in Figure 2, the length of the zero-area interval from x=0 to x=5 is the length of AB, giving AB=5. When P reaches the upper side of the rectangle, especially at point C, the height from point P to AB is equal to BC; at this time the area of triangle ABP reaches the maximum value 10. So there is y = (1/2)·AB·BC = 10, namely (1/2)×5×BC=10, solving gives BC=4. The length of the diagonal BD of the rectangle satisfies the Pythagorean theorem: BD = sqrt(AB^2+BC^2)=sqrt(5^2+4^2)=sqrt(41).
